about: Finite distinctions for claim collection, effective order, truth candidates and covering-cause event scope.

L1.equalTimestamp: The existing mark reading retains sequence order on ties; collections with equal timestamps and reversed widening/signature sequence are different effective orders, and may differ.

L3.truthHypothesis: Truth is one of these admissible singleton candidates; either candidate can be true. The fixture supplies no external evidence to select it.
L3.meaning: Swapping claim arrival cannot resolve an empty meet. Choosing either branch can discard the truth in one admissible assignment; this does not establish a normative rule without the truth-candidate hypothesis.

L7.meaning: All witnesses copy the common symbol when active; the private fixture copies truth deterministically when inactive. Active contribution c/n is q-independent by symmetry; total unanimity includes private contribution and is not c/n. This finite counterexample does not define a general factor-governance model.
L7.conditionalMarginalDerivation: Under uniform truth and a symmetric active n-ary channel, P(Y=v|C=1)=(q+(n-1)*(1-q)/(n-1))/n=1/n. Copies add no new event condition. Multiplication by P(C=1)=c yields the joint active contribution, not the unconditioned whole-mixture event.

L8-L9.scope: Existing M/3 identification uses handed sharing sets and truth-labelled population correctness moments. Positive correctness, full shared-factor column rank, compatible moments and the declared budget are required; singleton/private decomposition stays unresolved. Dissent excludes only a specific ordered configuration. No general partial symmetric-cause q identification iff outsider theorem is supplied by these functions.
L8-L9.linearizationUnderHandedM3: For positive correctness and compatible handed independent factor survivals, log(P(correct_a,correct_b)/(P(correct_a)P(correct_b))) is the sum of negative log survivals for factors shared by a and b. Full column rank identifies those shared log survivals in this model; singleton/private causes do not supply shared columns and remain unresolved. Zero correctness or incompatible moments invalidates this linearization even with the same declared sharing matrix.
